diagnostic_evidence.quote: When $\kappa$ is the squared exponential kernel, there exists a scalar $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $\bar{\kappa} = \lambda \kappa$

issues.failure_explanation: The general MSIP map is Ψ_MSIP(Y) = W(Y)^{-1} κ̄(Y)^{-1} v̂1(Y) and the general gradient identity is ∇F_M = W(κ̄WY − v̂1). For the squared exponential kernel κ̄ = λκ (λ = 1/σ²), substitution gives Ψ_MSIP(Y) = λ^{-1} W(Y)^{-1} K(Y)^{-1} vonem(Y) and ∇F_M = λWKWY − Wvonem = λWKW(Y − Ψ_MSIP). The printed specializations drop the scalar: the Gaussian MSIP update in sec:msip is printed without λ^{-1}, and eq:gradien_opt_mmd_gaussian_kernel is printed without λ. As printed, the Gaussian map's fixed points are not critical points of F_M, and the Gaussian gradient formula is false by the factor λ.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the factor λ^{-1} in the Gaussian MSIP map, ytplus = λ^{-1} W(yt)^{-1} K(yt)^{-1} vonem(yt), and the factor λ in eq:gradien_opt_mmd_gaussian_kernel, ∇F_M(y) = λ W(y) K(y) W(y) (y − Ψ_MSIP(y)); equivalently, retain the general κ̄-based forms, which are correct.
issues.overall_effect: The two Gaussian-kernel specializations — the MSIP update map (the kernel actually used in the numerics, with σ = 5) and the Gaussian form of the gradient identity inside thm:gradient_opt_mmd — are wrong by the constant factor λ = 1/σ² (equivalently its inverse in the map). The general theory is intact.
issues.title: Gaussian specializations drop the scalar factor λ
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-line insertion of an explicit constant in two displays. The general identity ∇F_M = W(κ̄WY − v̂1), the preconditioned-gradient-descent interpretation with M = Wκ̄W, and the mean-shift corollary are all correct and unaffected, so no claim, guarantee, or regime is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof differentiates the kernel mean embedding under the integral sign, writing ∇_{ij}v0(yi) = ∫ ∇_{ij}κ(x,yi) dπ(x), and explicitly invokes boundedness of ∇κ, while the theorem statement assumes only assumption:gradient_kappa. Moreover, the statement's own quantities v̄0(y) = ∫ κ̄(x,y) dπ and v̄1(y) = ∫ x κ̄(x,y) dπ require the same integrability. The paper imposes this hypothesis in prop:steady_state_equation_on_y but not in the theorem, so as stated the theorem is not established (and its formula may be ill-defined) for kernels with unbounded gradient.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis 'and the gradient of κ is bounded on X' (equivalently, that the kernel mean embedding v0 is differentiable on X) to the statement of thm:gradient_opt_mmd; the proof then goes through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, thm:gradient_opt_mmd is unproved for kernels whose gradient is unbounded on X; cor:ms_as_MSIP inherits the gap because its proof is given as a direct consequence of the theorem.
issues.title: thm:gradient_opt_mmd omits the bounded-gradient hypothesis its proof needs
issues.why_classification: A one-line hypothesis addition repairs the gap; all kernels used in the paper (Gaussian, Matérn, IMQ) satisfy it, and every conclusion and downstream result is preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: Differentiating the established expression F_M = ½(C_π − ⟨ŵ,Kŵ⟩) gives 2∇_{ij}F_M = −2⟨ŵ,K∇_{ij}ŵ⟩ − ⟨ŵ,(∇_{ij}K)ŵ⟩, the opposite of the printed eq:gradient_optimal_mmd_identity. The printed eq:grad_F_pi_first consequently has flipped signs, and the correctly signed eq:2times_gradient_FM does not follow from it; the proof also contains the earlier typo F_M = ½(C_π + 2⟨ŵ,v0⟩ + ⟨ŵ,Kŵ⟩) (the +2 should be −2, as the immediately following simplification confirms). Taken literally, the printed derivation yields ∇F_M = W(v̂1 − κ̄WY), the negative of the claimed identity. The two sign errors cancel, so the final assembly and the theorem statement are correct (verified independently, e.g., via the M=1 corollary), but the printed proof is internally inconsistent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the signs in eq:gradient_optimal_mmd_identity and eq:grad_F_pi_first (and change +2⟨ŵ,v0⟩ to −2⟨ŵ,v0⟩ in the expansion of F_M); the remainder of the proof then follows as printed.
issues.overall_effect: The printed proof of the paper's central gradient identity contains a false displayed differentiation identity and a non-sequitur between consecutive displays; the theorem's statement and all downstream uses (preconditioned gradient descent, mean-shift corollary) remain valid because the final result is correct.
issues.title: Sign errors in the printed derivation of ∇F_M inside the proof of thm:gradient_opt_mmd
issues.why_classification: The corrections are forced sign flips localized to a few displays, with no new lemma or argument needed; the final statement is correct and independently verifiable, so no mathematical content, claim, or guarantee is lost.
